plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'Limitations of Liability'; check whether the cap is mutual, tied to fees paid, and whether carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct, indemnity obligations) are preserved.
Section 7 provides indemnification of Contractor, i.e., running the wrong direction; a vendor-side IP/misconduct indemnity appears absent and should be added while narrowing our indemnity.
No restrictive covenant section in the outline; scan the purpose/engagement scope in Section 1 for any limitation on competing products or services before concluding it is absent.
No exclusivity heading; check Section 1 (purpose of engagement) for sole-source or exclusive-provider language.
Pricing sits in Section 3 (Contractor's Compensation); confirm there is no most-favoured-customer obligation flowing from us to Contractor.
No dedicated personnel or general provisions section is listed; check the engagement scope and termination provisions for any hiring restriction on us.
Section 6 (Termination) is the home for convenience rights; verify we may terminate on short notice without penalty and that Contractor cannot terminate at will mid-engagement.
Term provisions are not in the visible outline (Section 2 is not surfaced); look in Section 6 for renewal or evergreen language and any notice window and price escalator.

No general/miscellaneous provisions section appears; if governing law and venue are truly absent we should propose an approved forum, otherwise it may be tucked into the closing paragraphs near Section 7.
No assignment heading in the outline; check Section 6 for any change-of-control termination trigger and add affiliate/successor assignment rights for us.

Section 4 governs ownership of materials and acceptance; confirm work product and our data vest in us on creation (not on payment) and that no Clear Capital IP is assigned or licensed to Contractor beyond performing the Services.
Any licence-back or retained-tools licence should sit in Section 4; ensure it extends to our affiliates and contractors and is perpetual/irrevocable rather than revocable at will.
No audit heading; check Sections 3 and 4 for inspection or verification rights over our records or usage, and if present add notice, frequency and cost limits.
Look for penalty, late fee or liquidated damages language in the compensation section and in the liability section; credits in our favour are acceptable, damages against us are not.

Section 5 pairs Contractor warranties with a disclaimer; test the warranty period, conformity to Specifications, and whether the remedy is real rather than gutted by the disclaimer. Coordinate with acceptance in Section 4.
No insurance section is listed; if Contractor personnel touch our systems or premises we should add standard coverage requirements, likely alongside Section 5 representations.
Check Section 3 compensation terms for minimum fees, guaranteed hours or non-refundable retainers that operate as a take-or-pay without an exit.
Section 6 termination effects and Section 4 ownership are the natural homes; confirm whether return of deliverables and data plus wind-down assistance is addressed, and add it if not.
